notes: Managed settings apply to every project on the machine, and a deny rule from any settings file wins over an allow.
Claude Code's docs say Bash rules match the command as written, not the program: git -C . push and sh -c '...' get past a Bash(git push *) rule. The selfhost hook checks every Bash call as well.
The hooks run the same command selfhost agents configure writes, and Claude Code runs identical handlers once.
allowManagedMcpServersOnly makes this the only MCP allowlist: allowlists in user and project settings are ignored.

rules.detail: Bash rules cover every command the regular expression matches. Claude Code also applies them to each part of a compound command and looks through wrappers such as timeout, so they block a little more.

Bash rules cover every command the regular expression matches. Claude Code also applies them to each part of a compound command and looks through wrappers such as timeout, so they block a little more.

The regular expression has no ^, and Claude Code matches each command after taking off wrappers such as timeout and leading VAR=value, so rm -rf inside those is missed. The selfhost hook checks the rest.
Claude Code matches commands by prefix and * wildcards, and the regular expression uses quantifier .*. The selfhost hook checks it.
Claude Code reads ./ from the folder a session starts in and selfhost reads paths from the repository root, so a session started in a subfolder is missed. The selfhost hook checks the rest.

Claude Code reads ./ from the folder a session starts in and selfhost reads paths from the repository root, so a session started in a subfolder is missed. Edit rules also cover Write and NotebookEdit. The selfhost hook checks the rest.
WebFetch domain wildcards need Claude Code 2.1.172 or later. The selfhost hook checks it.
Observe mode: nothing native is written until the rule is enforced. A bare WebSearch rule covers every call to the tool. The selfhost hook records its hits.
The rule is only for Codex.
allowedMcpServers, made the only MCP allowlist by allowManagedMcpServersOnly, blocks every other server name. Like selfhost, it trusts the name the user gave the server.
